facts.raw_span: A woman in her 60s with a history of hypertension
sudden-onset chest pain
no history of any acute febrile illness
no family history of sudden cardiac death
tachycardic with a pulse of 120 beats/min
blood pressure was normal
White blood cell count: 14,300/µL
Serum calcium: within normal limits
High-sensitivity troponin I: 1.15 ng/mL
Brain-type natriuretic peptide: 1060.30 pg/mL
Initial ECG showed sinus tachycardia, PR-segment elevation in lead aVR, PR-segment depression in leads I, II, III, aVF, and V4 to V6
Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT: revealed an enhanced left-adrenal heterogeneous mass measuring 4.1 × 3.4 cm

blood pressure was normal
White blood cell count: 14,300/µL
Serum calcium: within normal limits
High-sensitivity troponin I: 1.15 ng/mL
Brain-type natriuretic peptide: 1060.30 pg/mL
Initial ECG showed sinus tachycardia, PR-segment elevation in lead aVR, PR-segment depression in leads I, II, III, aVF, and V4 to V6
Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT: revealed an enhanced left-adrenal heterogeneous mass measuring 4.1 × 3.4 cm

concepts.why: The patient presented with sudden-onset chest pain, elevated troponin, and characteristic ECG changes, which are consistent with Takotsubo cardiomyopathy.
The patient has an enhanced left-adrenal heterogeneous mass, which is suggestive of pheochromocytoma.
The patient presented with chest pain and elevated troponin, which are consistent with myocardial infarction.
The patient has an adrenal mass, which could be causing adrenal crisis.
The patient presented with chest pain, elevated troponin, and stress-induced ECG changes, which are consistent with stress-induced cardiomyopathy.
The patient has a history of hypertension and presented with normal blood pressure, but the condition could be related to hypertensive emergency.

rationales.F01: Hypertension is a risk factor for various cardiovascular conditions.
rationales.F02: Sudden-onset chest pain is a common symptom of acute coronary syndromes and other cardiac conditions.
rationales.F05: Tachycardia can be a sign of various conditions, including cardiac and adrenal disorders.
rationales.F09: Elevated troponin levels indicate myocardial injury.
rationales.F10: Elevated BNP levels are associated with heart failure and other cardiac conditions.
rationales.F11: ECG findings are consistent with myocardial infarction and other cardiac conditions.
rationales.F12: The presence of an adrenal mass suggests pheochromocytoma or other adrenal disorders.

frontier_selector.rationale: systolic apical ballooning and ECG changes with normal coronary arteries support Takotsubo cardiomyopathy, while the adrenal mass could be an incidental finding
